hypotheses.claim: An account created through Settings -> Users cannot log in: no user_credentials row is ever written outside seed code, so the console's only provisioning path produces a dead account.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: A hook, subscriber or auth-side listener mints the credential on user creation, or login falls back to a first-time set-password path when credential is null.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -rn 'userCredential\.' --include=*.ts --exclude-dir=generated apps/backend/src -> only credential-seed.ts:17,21; grep -rn 'ensureCredential' -> auth-fixture-seed.ts:141 and dev-seed.ts only. No org/ caller.

hypotheses.claim: GET /api/org/geo/{states,regions,districts} answer 200 to a SERVICE_ENGINEER token — AuthGuard without RoleGuard means every authenticated role reads the geography reference set.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: A global APP_GUARD RoleGuard applies a default deny to undecorated handlers, making the missing @Roles inert.
hypotheses.altCheck: static.md totals line: 4 endpoints with no @Roles, 0 @Public; geography.controller.ts:12 declares @UseGuards(AuthGuard) only — RoleGuard is not in the decorator list, unlike every other org/ controller.

hypotheses.claim: Deactivating a plant removes stops from an SE's live day plan with no push, no outbox row and no in-app notice — the SE keeps driving to a site whose ticket is already CLOSED.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: The mobile day-plan read is live enough that the stop simply vanishes on next poll, or a generic ticket-cancelled notifier fires off the ticket_events row written at :188.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -rln 'notificationOutbox|NotificationOutbox' apps/backend/src -> only scheduling/day-plan-notification-outbox.ts and business-sweep-scheduler.service.ts; plant-deactivation/ appears in neither.

hypotheses.claim: A threshold changed by the CSM at 09:00 governs the 10:00 dispatch run, and that run's config_snapshot stores the new number — the value in force is recoverable per run.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: The dispatch path caches the threshold at module init, so the snapshot records the fresh DB row while the engine ran on a stale in-process copy — snapshot right, behaviour wrong.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -rn 'SE_ASSIGNMENT_THRESHOLD_KEY' --exclude-dir=generated apps/backend/src -> 4 hits, all reads at call time (dispatch-run.service.ts:1331 inside captureConfigSnapshot, setting-authority.ts:18, settings.service.ts:15,41); no module-scope cache found.

hypotheses.claim: A ZONAL_MANAGER calling PUT /api/settings/assignment-threshold is refused (class @Roles is OH+CSM, and canWriteSetting refuses ZM independently), so the graded party genuinely cannot move its own dial.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: The handler-level @Roles on the GET (:69, which adds ZONAL_MANAGER) overrides at class scope in this Nest setup, admitting ZM to every route on the controller — which is exactly how static.md read it.
hypotheses.altCheck: sed -n '55,105p' assignment-threshold.controller.ts: ZONAL_MANAGER appears only on the @Get handler; @Put carries no @Roles, and the class decorator lists OH,CSM. static.md row 48 attributes ZM to the PUT — one of the two readings is wrong and only a call settles it.
